original_title: A field study of the impacts of workplace diversity on the recruitment of minority group members
evidence: Focuses on original Analysis 1 applicant composition. Reconstructed code reproduces primary estimates; clustered standard errors and multinomial logit leave conclusions unchanged. Power simulation scripts differ from stated sample size/probability settings and give unstable results; report concludes these issues do not undermine primary findings.
limitations: No new participants. Power discrepancy is not established as a consequential error in substantive estimates. Report conflates RStudio build identifiers with R versions, weakening its proposed environment explanation; no independent rerun here.

original_title: A field study of the impacts of workplace diversity on the recruitment of minority group members
evidence: Reproduces original three analyses using Stata rather than R/SPSS. Exclusion-threshold rounding gives 1,597 instead of 1,585 observations but negligible estimate changes. Diversity-cue findings persist. Exploratory gender difference in applicant quality attenuates after controlling rater and job domain; this concerns a different conditional comparison, not a demonstrated coding error.
limitations: Authors acknowledge interpretation depends on job selection, without establishing that adjustment is the uniquely correct estimand. Response is evidence within this unit, not an additional independent assessment.

original_title: The Gender Gap in Self-Promotion
evidence: Main male-typed-task self-evaluation gap reproduces and survives multiplicity correction. Additional samples reveal gender differences in financial deservingness for verbal tasks. Alternative wage-censoring approaches increase estimated premiums, but conclusion explicitly calls original approach valid and conservative.
limitations: No new data; additional samples/outcomes and censoring specifications do not establish an original error. Original raw-data/cleaning completeness limits reconstruction.

original_title: The Gender Gap in Self-Promotion
evidence: Precisely reproduces original Tables II–IV with no coding/rounding errors. Multiple-testing corrections and ordered logit support primary findings. Within-sample adjustment for beliefs weakens significance, while pooled and experimental-information comparisons retain gaps.
limitations: Analysis starts from final shared data; lack of raw-data reconstruction is not evidence of an error. Belief-adjusted models address a different comparison.

original_title: Accuracy and social motivations shape judgements of (mis)information
evidence: Reproduces most original findings after code adjustments. Authors acknowledge small rounding/p-value/effect-size discrepancies without changed main conclusions. Mixed item/subject models weaken some effects and show a false-news accuracy tradeoff. Alleged large partisan-gap discrepancy compares different groups; Tukey discrepancies reflect different contrast families, so neither establishes a verified material error.
limitations: No new participants. Alternative Bayesian/mixed models and differing multiple-testing families are not coded as original errors. Response disputes some reproduction discrepancies; minor acknowledged ones are distinguished from those disputes.

original_title: Accuracy and social motivations shape judgements of (mis)information
evidence: Original findings reproduce computationally after minor fixes. New Study 4 replication N = 1,378, fielded May 2025, yields smaller effects; preregistered Tukey-adjusted binary-outcome contrasts generally fail significance, while unadjusted contrasts and continuous-scale financial-incentive contrasts retain some significance. This is attenuation and inconclusive replication, not proof all effects vanish.
evidence_locator: Revised assessment PDF pp.4-10,15-17; response pp.1-4
limitations: Report footnote 4 acknowledges a coding error in an earlier REPLICATION draft that original authors helped correct. Do not attribute that error to Rathje et al. Original-author response predates revised report and compares unadjusted p-values. Stimuli/time and outcome coding differ in specified ways.

original_title: Seeing racial avoidance on New York City streets
evidence: Published results reproduce; much distributed figure code replots supplied statistics. Excluding extreme pedestrian distances attenuates estimates; alternative bootstrap seeds do not. Analytic clustered errors change one unadjusted specification. Authors explain extreme distances reflect physical site bounds, so exclusion is not a demonstrated error correction.
limitations: No new field data. Same-assessment identity verified by title, author and 81/81 shared normalized 200-character text blocks. Missing analysis code limits reproduction depth but does not establish original error.

original_title: Seeing racial avoidance on New York City streets
evidence: New Berlin 3D-video experiment compares distance to racialized Muslim bystanders and White bystanders. Pooled direction supports avoidance, but effects vary across streets and conventional clustered versus wild-bootstrap inference. Conclusion calls for more randomly selected sites, not correction of original NYC analysis.
limitations: Different setting, minoritized group, observation technology and available covariates. Same team/report verified against DP250 by title/authors and 87 shared normalized 200-character blocks; discussion-paper version is not a second assessment.

original_title: An umbrella review of randomized control trials on the effects of physical exercise on cognition

Updated replicator note accepts resolution.
